s_9fe9390105ff5e70.k: dual_reader_concordant_negative_presence_stop Task-level procedure for binary lung-abnormality presence questions on a single frontal chest radiograph: obtain one targeted expert yes/no read and one grounded report; stop with a negative response only when both independently show no abnormality and no grounded boxes.

c.name: dual_reader_concordant_negative_presence_stop
c.description: Task-level procedure for binary lung-abnormality presence questions on a single frontal chest radiograph: obtain one targeted expert yes/no read and one grounded report; stop with a negative response only when both independently show no abnormality and no grounded boxes.
c.applicable_conditions: Question type/object: binary yes/no presence question about any abnormality in the lung fields on a single frontal chest radiograph. Triggering evidence: an appropriate full-image chest X-ray expert VQA call to an abnormality presence query returns an unambiguous negative answer, and a grounded report call on the same image returns a report equivalent to no significant findings with grounded_box_count = 0. Exclusions: not for laterality/side, localization, extent, severity, comparison/interval change, specific-diagnosis, non-binary, multi-image, non-frontal, or non-chest-radiograph questions; do not conclude negative from a single reader, a bare yes/no, a crop, or a coordinate box alone; do not apply if either output is positive, equivocal, truncated, missing, failed, contains any finding, or contains any grounded box. Required tool capabilities: one registered tool able to answer a targeted abnormality presence question over the same full image, and one registered grounded report tool able to generate a report with explicit grounded findings/boxes on the same image. Stopping/unknown condition: the negative stop is valid only for concordant negative outputs with zero grounded boxes; if outputs are discordant, uncertain, incomplete, or fail, do not emit a negative conclusion from the stop rule—perform at most one targeted observed verification if available, otherwise return unknown/insufficient evidence.
c.core_action: 1) Verify the question is a binary presence question about lung abnormality on one frontal chest radiograph; if it asks side, location, extent, severity, change, or another object, stop and do not apply this skill. 2) Call chest_xray_expert once with a targeted yes/no abnormality query over the full image. 3) Call maira2_grounded_report once with no arguments on the same image. 4) Inspect the observable outputs: the expert answer must be unambiguously negative, and the grounded report must state no significant findings with grounded_box_count = 0. 5) If both checks pass, emit the negative presence response and stop; do not escalate to ROI crop, phrase grounding, or additional readers. 6) If either output is positive, equivocal, incomplete, truncated, or fails, or if any finding/box is present, do not infer negative from concordance; if a specific unresolved discrepancy remains, perform one targeted observed verification with available registered tools and stop when resolved. If still unresolved, return unknown/insufficient evidence rather than a negative answer.

c.name: Skeletal Abnormality Presence Corroboration
c.description: For chest X-ray VQA questions asking whether the skeletal system is abnormal, use a targeted skeletal expert query followed by independent grounded-report corroboration. Answer absence only when both sources explicitly negate acute osseous/skeletal abnormality, and keep incidental non-skeletal findings separate from the skeletal judgment.
c.applicable_conditions: Applies to chest X-ray VQA items that ask a yes/no presence question about skeletal-system abnormality and whose options encode presence versus absence. Triggering evidence: the question explicitly names the skeletal system or osseous abnormality. Required tool capabilities: a registered chest X-ray expert capable of answering a targeted skeletal query enumerating fractures, lytic lesions, and deformities, plus a registered grounded reporting tool capable of independently emitting an osseous/skeletal statement. Exclusions: not for non-skeletal questions, differential diagnosis, severity grading, measurements, or patient identity; not sufficient for laterality/region localization or lesion counting, which require an explicit side/region query with an unknown outcome because a bare yes/no, crop, or coordinate box alone cannot resolve side; do not use when neither required tool is available or when only non-skeletal corroboration exists.
c.core_action: Parse the question to confirm that the object is skeletal/osseous abnormality and that the required response is yes/no presence. Call chest_xray_expert with a targeted skeletal question enumerating fractures, lytic lesions, and deformities. Inspect its response for a clear skeletal/osseous answer. If the expert response is affirmative, call maira2_grounded_report on the same image and inspect its findings/report for at least one explicit skeletal/osseous statement about the same image (for example sternotomy, deformity, or fracture); keep incidental non-skeletal findings from other systems out of the target judgment. If such an explicit skeletal/osseous statement is present, answer the option denoting presence and stop. If the expert response is clearly negative, call maira2_grounded_report on the same image for independent corroboration and inspect the report for an explicit osseous statement; if both sources independently state no acute osseous changes or skeletal abnormality, answer the option denoting absence and stop. Do not treat incidental non-skeletal findings, such as soft-tissue density, as skeletal abnormalities. If the expert response is equivocal, if the report lacks an explicit osseous statement for the queried skeletal question, if a source fails, or if the sources conflict about the same finding and image, do not claim absence or presence from that discordance; perform at most one additional targeted observed verification on the same skeletal question/image with a registered suitable tool if available, then if still unresolved state unknown/uncertain when the answer format permits, otherwise avoid asserting abnormality or absence beyond the observed evidence. Stop once an affirmative expert plus an explicit skeletal/osseous report statement supports presence, or both independent skeletal-specific statements agree on absence, or after the single conflict/unknown verification has been attempted and no resolution is obtained. Keep unexecuted steps as hypotheses.

s_a3ec4f056cf659b7.k: Targeted structure-presence verification with report scope check Use an exact-question targeted expert for binary disease-presence questions about a named anatomical structure, and explicitly scope-check any broader grounded report before citing it as confirmation.

c.name: Targeted structure-presence verification with report scope check
c.description: Use an exact-question targeted expert for binary disease-presence questions about a named anatomical structure, and explicitly scope-check any broader grounded report before citing it as confirmation.
c.applicable_conditions: Question type/object: binary disease or abnormality presence question about a specific named anatomical structure (for example, pleura) on a chest image. Triggering evidence: the question names the structure, and a broad grounded report may be used to corroborate a targeted expert answer; the report may explicitly address the queried structure. Exclusions: laterality/side questions, region-localization questions, multi-structure or global-impression questions. Do not treat an unmentioned structure as normal or as target-specific confirmation. Required tool capabilities: a targeted VQA/expert tool that accepts an exact anatomical question and returns an answer, plus, if used, a broad grounded report tool that returns free-text findings. Unknown handling: if the targeted tool fails or is ambiguous and no report explicitly covers the structure, report insufficient evidence or unknown rather than inferring from unrelated normal findings.
c.core_action: Ask the targeted expert the exact structure-specific presence question and record whether the answer is clear yes/no or ambiguous. If using a broader grounded report for corroboration, inspect its findings/report for an explicit statement about that same named structure; statements about lungs, heart, mediastinum, pleura, or skeleton are not structure-specific confirmation. If the report explicitly addresses the structure and agrees, cite it as corroboration; if it conflicts, obtain another targeted observed check or report uncertainty. If the report omits the structure, do not cite it as target-specific confirmation and either rely on a clear targeted-expert answer or obtain another targeted check. If the targeted answer is unclear or fails and no explicit report statement covers the structure, stop and state unknown/insufficient evidence. Stop when the targeted expert is clear and any cited corroborating report explicitly covers the queried structure without conflict, or when unknown/insufficient evidence is declared.

s_47c17dd2fe9a6a60.k: Cardiovascular system presence check on chest radiographs with concordant expert and report absence For yes/no chest-radiograph VQA questions asking whether the cardiovascular system shows any abnormal signs, name the relevant cardinal cardiovascular abnormalities in an explicit expert query, then obtain an independent grounded report for corroboration. Use concordant absence only when the named abnormality list is sufficiently comprehensive for the question and the report explicitly supports no significant findings; otherwise stop unresolved.

c.name: Cardiovascular system presence check on chest radiographs with concordant expert and report absence
c.description: For yes/no chest-radiograph VQA questions asking whether the cardiovascular system shows any abnormal signs, name the relevant cardinal cardiovascular abnormalities in an explicit expert query, then obtain an independent grounded report for corroboration. Use concordant absence only when the named abnormality list is sufficiently comprehensive for the question and the report explicitly supports no significant findings; otherwise stop unresolved.
c.applicable_conditions: Applies only to presence-type visual question answering with yes/no options on a chest radiograph whose object is the cardiovascular system or 'any cardiovascular signs' using broad system-level wording. Triggering evidence: the question is broad/system-level for cardiovascular findings, and a chest radiograph is available. Before querying, the expert prompt must name the cardinal cardiovascular abnormalities relevant to the question, anchored to source-supported examples such as cardiomegaly, vascular congestion, and aortic calcification; the list must be sufficiently comprehensive for the question's scope. Required tool capabilities: a chest-radiograph expert QA model that accepts an explicit abnormality-list question, and an independent grounded-report/report-generation tool for the same image that returns a report or 'no significant findings'. Exclusions: do not apply to laterality/side questions, non-chest-radiograph images, or questions about a specific single finding where broad-system absence is not at issue. Do not use a bare yes/no, crop, or coordinate box to resolve side. Do not treat an incomplete abnormality list, a single negative model output, or a report limited to unrelated findings as evidence of absence. Stopping/unknown: stop and select the negative option only when both tools complete and concordantly report absence of the named cardiovascular abnormalities and the independent report explicitly supports no significant findings or no significant cardiovascular findings for the same image. If either tool fails, is unavailable, returns ambiguous output, or the outputs conflict, do not assume absence; if a conflict concerns the same finding and image, perform at most one targeted observed verification with a registered tool; if still unresolved, or if the named list cannot be made sufficiently comprehensive, stop and mark unresolved.
c.core_action: 1) Confirm the item is a yes/no presence question about the cardiovascular system on a chest radiograph; otherwise stop as not applicable. 2) Reformulate it into an explicit expert question listing the cardinal cardiovascular abnormalities relevant to the question, using source-supported examples such as cardiomegaly, vascular congestion, and aortic calcification, and verify the list is sufficiently comprehensive; if not, stop unresolved. 3) Call chest_xray_expert with that explicit abnormality-list question. 4) Call maira2_grounded_report on the same image to obtain an independent report. 5) Compare only observable outputs: require both calls to complete; require the expert to report absence of the named abnormalities; require the report to state no significant findings or no significant cardiovascular findings. If these concordant-absence conditions hold, select the negative option and stop. 6) If either call fails or is unavailable, if the report is ambiguous, if the named list is incomplete, or if outputs conflict, do not infer absence. For a conflict about the same finding and image, allow at most one targeted observed verification using a registered tool; if unresolved, stop and report uncertainty rather than asserting absence.

s_f7e34347ccc64ea7.k: binary-thoracic-disease-negative-verification A targeted verification procedure for binary thoracic disease-presence questions: obtain a direct expert answer, and only when it is negative, corroborate with a structured grounded report before finalizing the negative response.

c.name: binary-thoracic-disease-negative-verification
c.description: A targeted verification procedure for binary thoracic disease-presence questions: obtain a direct expert answer, and only when it is negative, corroborate with a structured grounded report before finalizing the negative response.
c.applicable_conditions: Applicable only to a binary yes/no question asking whether any disease or acute thoracic abnormality is present in the thorax on a single provided chest radiograph. Triggering evidence is an initial chest_xray_expert answer that clearly says no/negative for thoracic disease. Requires a direct CXR VQA/expert tool able to answer the same binary question and a structured grounded-report tool able to produce findings or a report for the same image. Exclude disease-specific presence questions, nonbinary questions, laterality/side/localization/severity/comparison/management questions, non-thoracic questions, and cases where the initial expert answer is positive or unusable; for laterality, use a separate explicit side/region query with an unknown outcome.
c.core_action: 1) Call chest_xray_expert on the same image with the binary thoracic disease-presence question. 2) Inspect the returned answer: only a clear negative/no response activates the verification path; if the answer is positive, non-binary, empty, or an error, stop this skill and do not use the negative-verification sequence. 3) For a clear negative, call maira2_grounded_report on the same image. 4) Review its findings/report for acute thoracic abnormalities; clear lungs, normal heart size, and no acute osseous abnormality corroborate absence, while non-thoracic incidental hardware or other non-thoracic findings do not count as thoracic disease. 5) If the structured report corroborates absence of acute thoracic findings, select the negative option and stop. 6) If the report is unavailable, failed, or inconclusive, or if it lists an acute thoracic finding despite the expert's negative answer, stop without forcing a negative answer and mark the result unresolved/unknown unless a further observed check is available.
